thesis: Insulet (Nasdaq: PODD) came out of the annual screen as a growth and quality lead. Q3 2026 10-Q (balance sheet, income statement, revenue discussion read; MD&A truncated after R&D and SG&A): Q3 revenue 842.0M (US Omnipod 570.4M +14.7%, international 266.2M +31.7%, Drug Delivery 5.5M), 9M revenue 2,405.4M (+25.0% vs 1,924.3M), gross profit 9M 1,723.8M (71.7%), operating income Q3 189.8M, 9M net income 327.1M (vs 145.5M), diluted EPS Q3 2.03. Effective tax rate fell to 20.0% for 9M from 27.0%, which adds roughly 29M to 9M net income versus the old rate (my estimate). 9M includes a 38.5M net cost for a voluntary cannula correction (about 50M total expected) and a 7.0M warranty reserve release in Q3. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 584.4M; debt 962.2M (Term Loan B 473.8M, notes 450.0M, plant and equipment financing about 50M), net debt 377.8M; liabilities 1,836.0M; equity 1,579.1M. TTM (FY2025 10-K plus 9M26 less 9M25): revenue 3,189.2M, net income 428.7M, OCF 509.0M, capex 249.0M, FCF 260.0M, SBC 81.8M, FCF after SBC 178.2M. Price: close 145.34 on 2026-11-17 x 69,371,043 shares (10-Q cover, 2026-10-27) = 10.08B market cap = 23.5x TTM net income, FCF yield 2.6% (1.8% after SBC), EV about 10.46B. Stock fell from 152.48 (11-13) to 145.34 (11-17), cause not identified. 9M buybacks 300M and a new 1B authorization in October. Growth of 25% at about 24x earnings is not demanding on its face, but FCF is small because of capex and the multiple leans on a reduced tax rate; a quality and growth lead, not a demonstrated mispricing.
counterthesis: Earnings are helped by a tax rate down 7 points and a warranty release; at the old rate TTM earnings would be lower, so the multiple is higher than 23x. FCF yield 2.6% (1.8% after SBC) is low because capex is large (249M TTM, 113.9M in 9M26 versus 56.5M a year earlier). Debt 962M plus a 1B buyback authorization raises leverage if funded with debt. A cannula tear correction signals product quality risk; a securities class action (Hu v. Insulet, filed 2026-07-02) and the tariff exemption for medical devices are open risks. Competition in automated insulin delivery, GLP-1 effects on diabetes demand, and reimbursement were not reviewed (MD&A truncated). US growth slowed to 14.7% versus 31.7% international.
invalidation: Invalidated if US Omnipod growth falls below about 10% with margin pressure, if corrections or recalls recur, if the tax rate reverts toward 27% with flat pretax income, if capex stays above 8% of revenue without FCF growth, or if debt rises to fund buybacks while FCF after SBC stays under 2% of market cap.
